title: 3-Read Friday #68: Learning Barriers, CPD Checklists, and Active Learning
author: Craig Barton
summary: Issue #68 of 3-Read Friday leads with Tom Sherrington's five common barriers to learning -- attention deficits, lack of prior knowledge, cognitive overload and transience, poor fluency of recall, and task completion as a false proxy for learning -- with Barton singling out cognitive overload and transience as his own blind spot. Adam Robbins follows with a detailed CPD session-planning checklist, including a worked example on introducing choral response, which Barton praises especially for its 'why this / why now / non-examples' structure. Claudia Lewis closes with an extended TikTok-dance analogy for why passive familiarity with content ('I've watched the video many times') is not the same as being able to independently perform it, translated into a chemistry classroom example of chunked, checked practice. Barton frames the issue around the shared theme of proxies that mislead teachers about whether real learning is happening -- attention that looks present but isn't secure, CPD that looks well-designed but skips a rationale step, and student familiarity that looks like mastery but isn't.
points: Sherrington's 'task completion is a poor proxy for learning' barrier warns that students can fill notebooks (copying diagrams, borrowing answers, matching definitions with a line) while doing almost no independent thinking -- the visible work product doesn't guarantee the invisible cognitive work happened.

Robbins's CPD checklist structures a session around 'Why this? Why now?' before any technique is introduced, forcing CPD leaders to justify the investment of teacher time before demonstrating the technique itself.

Robbins's 'non-example' step in a CPD session (showing a common misapplication of the technique, not just a correct example) is designed to sharpen teachers' conceptual boundaries around when a technique is and isn't being used correctly.

Lewis's TikTok dance analogy operationalizes into a concrete classroom method: chunk a multi-step process (like the moles = mass / Mr formula) into small pieces, check each piece before combining, and only then move to independent practice with increasing challenge.
quotes: Tom shares five issues that can hinder student learning. I need to be more aware of Cognitive overload and transience. The simple tweaks Tom suggests can greatly improve students' processing of information.
Adam shares a really useful checklist that can be used by teachers preparing to deliver CPD… or by teachers judging the effectiveness of the CPD they are receiving.
The whole thing is great, but I particularly liked the Why this, Why now, and Non-examples sections.
Claudia draws on her own experience learning a dance to reflect on the dangers of assuming that attentive students in our classrooms are truly learning.
